business_problem: Vale needed to improve maintenance, process control, and safety across mining, rail, pelletizing, and port operations by predicting failures earlier, reducing shutdowns and fuel use, and helping teams prioritize operational and health-and-safety actions across thousands of assets.
solution_summary: Vale built an Artificial Intelligence Center in Vitoria, Brazil, as an in-house hub to develop and monitor AI initiatives across ferrous metals, base metals, and coal operations. The implementation draws data from railroad infrastructure, mine equipment, pelletizing plants, employee demographics, and safety records. Named components in the source include waysides, which capture wheelset wear, impact, bearing temperature, noise, and bogie displacement, and AI systems and mathematical models that cross-check those feeds with information from other systems to predict failures and recommend actions. Vale also applies AI techniques to mine-equipment data and pellet-production data to extend tire and powertrain life, optimize fuel and energy use, and identify ideal operating conditions. Results are served to maintenance teams, plant operators, and health-and-safety professionals as predictions, risk scores, and operational recommendations that guide purchasing, maintenance scheduling, process tuning, and incident prevention.

data_flow: Data from railroad waysides, mine equipment, pelletizing production, employee demographics, and safety records is collected and cross-checked with information from other systems. Vale's AI systems and mathematical models analyze those inputs to predict fractures and asset failures, calculate incident risk, and generate operating recommendations for maintenance teams, plant operators, and health-and-safety professionals.
integration_points: Historical accidents, near misses, and unsafe-condition records
business_outcome: Vale says delivered AI projects generate more than US$20 million in annual savings, with another US$37 million in expected benefits from initiatives underway, while also improving rail safety, extending asset life, reducing plant costs, and helping teams prevent incidents.

evidence_quotes: "Vale uses AI systems to collect and analyze millions of data from its projects, generating insights that will help predict problems and influence decision making."
"Projects already delivered have generated more than US$20 million in savings per year and another US$37 million in benefits are expected from the initiatives that are underway."
"A set of sensors installed by the railroad called waysides monitor the wear as well as impact of wheelsets, temperature and noise of bearings, as well as displacements of the bogie."

"By cross-checking the data generated by these sensors with information from other systems, mathematical models were created to allow the maintenance team to predict the behavior of wheelsets in the following 30 days."

"The data generated is combined with historical accidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions of the localities. The system uses this information to calculate the probability of incidents occurring in each area in a specific period of time."
"These process improvements generated US$3 million in savings per year in one of the plants, in Vitoria. The gains came from a 7% reduction in variable costs"
